newsitem.title: USA: Musicland gets new term loan, lien waivers.
newsitem.headline: Musicland gets new term loan, lien waivers.

text.p: Musicland Stores Corp said Tuesday it had reached agreements with lenders for a new $50 million term loan, which along with other agreements will provide additional financing for the 1997 holiday season.
Musicland said it also received lien waivers from holders of subordinated debt, and paid its regularly scheduled interest payment on Monday.
"These agreements give Musicland time to realize the results of its streamlining and cost-cutting measures," said Reid Johnson, Musicland chief financial officer.
"Those measures are having a positive effect," he added. "Second-quarter-to-date EBITDA results (April-May) are ahead of last year and ahead of plan."
But Musicland said it still needs trade vendor support, in the form of normal credit terms, to have a successful holiday season.

The term loan is secured by Musicland's inventory, the company said. It can be drawn, subject to certain conditions, on September 15. It matures in February 1999, with 50 percent payable in December 1998 and 50 percent payable at maturity.
Lenders of the term loan received warrants equal to five percent of Musicland's fully diluted shares, at $1.56 a share, the company said.

It also amended its revolving credit facility. The change requires Musicland to reduce its overall revolving balance to $245 million by amortization payments of $20 million in December 1997 and $10 million in February 1998.
The amortization payments are secured by inventory, but only until the payments have been made, Musicland said.

The price for the warrants was set at 25 percent above the average of the closing price for the 10 days prior to May 8, the date that a tentative agreement on the term loan was approved by the steering committee of Musicland's bank group, it said.
The company also has received amendments to real estate loans relating to its Franklin distribution facility and three of its Media Play stores, it said.
